tagline: A higher-quality neural voice for every app — GPU-accelerated on-device, no key, no cloud.
description:
Offline Neural TTS (Kokoro) is a PROVIDER app: install it, keep it in your Providers folder, and assign it to the Text → speech AI type in Settings → AI models. From then on every app that asks GifOS to speak — Reader, games, anything using the ai ability — is answered by this app, entirely on your device.

The voice is Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0), an 82-million-parameter neural model with eight voices: Heart, Bella, Nicole, Sarah, Michael, Fenrir, Emma and George. It also answers to the familiar cloud names (nova, shimmer, fable, echo, onyx, alloy), so anything written for a cloud voice works unchanged.

GPU WHEN YOU HAVE ONE. Kokoro is a transformer whose maths runs well on a graphics chip, so this provider declares the GPU ability and runs on WebGPU where your device exposes one — and falls back to the CPU (WebAssembly) where it doesn't. Same voice either way; a real GPU just makes it think faster. Its tiny sibling, Offline Neural Text to Speech (KittenTTS), stays the instant, always-CPU option — pick whichever you prefer in Settings.

WHAT IT COSTS, PLAINLY. The engine rides inside the GIF, but the 163 MB fp16 voice model is downloaded once, checked against a SHA-256 fixed in the app, and kept on your computer. Because it is a neural model it thinks before it speaks: it generates a passage of audio before that passage can start playing, so there is a pause at the beginning of each one — shorter on a GPU, longer on a CPU, and longer the more text it is handed at once.

Once the voice is on your device it never asks the network again. The app itself cannot: a Provider app is refused any network capability at all, so nothing you ask it to say can leave this browser.
author: GifOS
